proposed_widenings.name: modify_roll_advantage.targetMarkedBySpellFilter
proposed_widenings.justification: The advantage applies only to attack rolls made against the creature currently bearing Hunter's Mark. The existing modify_roll_advantage atom has no field to scope the effect to the marked target. All current filters (attackerTypeFilter, skillFilter, conditionFilter, saveAbilityFilter, saveSourceFilter) constrain by attacker type, skill, condition, or save ability/source — none express 'the target that has spell X's mark on it'. A new optional field (e.g. markedBySpell: spellId, or a general targetStateFilter referencing the mark attachment) is needed.
proposed_widenings.evidence: You have Advantage on attack rolls against the creature currently marked by your Hunter's Mark.

notes: The passive family and class_feature kind fit correctly. The effect is a simple always-on modify_roll_advantage on attack_roll. The sole gap is target-side scoping: the advantage is restricted to attacks against the Hunter's Mark target, which is a cross-unit reference the current surface cannot represent without a new field on modify_roll_advantage. Encoding it without this field would produce a dishonest trace (advantage on ALL attack rolls, not just against the marked creature).
